applies_why: The judge text decides the Isaiah 7:14 issue as UNDERDETERMINED by splitting the verse into a wording answer from the challenger and a prophetic-application answer from the defender, which invokes the rule's bar on treating a two-sense verse as open.
quote: D5 vs C5 (Isaiah 7:14): UNDERDETERMINED -- Challenger answered the virgin and young-woman wording in [DR3] and defender answered the prophetic application in [CR2] and [CR3].
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.
room: The phrase A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.; I weighed reading it as allowing UNDERDETERMINED when each side answers a different sense or aspect of the verse, against reading it as requiring both senses to stand and forbidding UNDERDETERMINED on that basis.
why: The judge labels the Isaiah 7:14 issue UNDERDETERMINED because each side answered a different wording/application aspect, which treats the verse as open instead of letting both senses stand.
